clue.text: Flustered while visiting a sovereign country

definitions.meaning: someone flustered is agitated, in a tizzy
being within a nation's borders, literally inside a nation

explanation.surface: Someone gets agitated while on a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: the idiom for being agitated, and the literal sense of being inside a nation.

clue.text: He is undoubtedly a gossip, so watch!

definitions.meaning: a gossip passes on what was told to them again and again
a kind of pocket watch that chimes the hours when a button is pressed

explanation.surface: A remark that a talker is a gossip, with a warning to keep an eye on him.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip retells stories over and over, and a chiming pocket timepiece strikes the time again on demand.

clue.text: One who buys, or one who "sells"?

definitions.meaning: a customer in a store
an informer who sells out or betrays someone to the police; to shop is British slang for informing on

explanation.surface: A riddle contrasting buyer and seller.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shop' someone is British slang for betraying them to the police, which the quoted 'sells' (sells out) points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer purchases goods, and in British slang an informer who betrays others is said to shop them.

clue.text: Invent cosmetics

definitions.meaning: to make something up is to invent it (here as the phrase ...)
lipstick, powder and the like

explanation.definitionFit: Fabricating a story is a sense of the verb phrase, while the noun means facial cosmetics such as lipstick.

clue.text: Begins by putting pastry into large vessel

indicators.note: the pastry word is put into the vessel word, as the clue says

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a large vessel

explanation.surface: Instructions for a baker beginning by setting pastry in a big dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large vessel' sounds like a kitchen bowl, but it is a steamship, SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean commences, as a verb in the third person.

clue.text: Kindly offer to listen to Heath

parts.note: Ted Heath, British Prime Minister in the 1970s, was known as Ted

explanation.surface: A kind invitation to hear what the politician Heath has to say.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath, UK Prime Minister 1970-74, was widely called Ted, giving TED.
explanation.definitionFit: A compassionate, gentle person is described by both words.

clue.text: Nun acting as operational overseer?

parts.note: the theatre is the world of acting

explanation.surface: A nun takes on the role of supervisor of operations.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a 'sister' is a senior nurse; the one in charge of an operating theatre oversees operations.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse who supervises surgical operations, with 'operational' read as about surgery.

clue.text: Is soil found in barren areas and isolated spots on the map?

indicators.note: the clue says these words are found inside the word for barren areas

explanation.surface: A geography question about soil in arid places and remote spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninhabited islands are remote places marked alone on a chart.

clue.text: Tenant makes an ill-spoken request to view

indicators.note: badly pronounced, so the phrase meant is sounded carelessly

parts.note: let's see is a request to look at something

explanation.surface: A tenant asks clumsily to look round a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's see' said slurred drops the T and runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who holds a lease is a renter of property.

clue.text: Pastry table design

definitions.meaning: the baked casing of a pie
a style of small table with a scalloped raised edge resembling a crimped pie edge

explanation.surface: A bakery item and furniture style side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: A piecrust table is an 18th-century style of tilt-top table whose rim is carved like a crimped pie edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The pie's baked shell, and a furniture style whose scalloped rim imitates it.

clue.text: A record peak

explanation.surface: A record reaching the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain, especially in Switzerland, is a high summit.

clue.text: A cobbler is apparently working after all

definitions.meaning: a cobbler shapes shoes on a last, so one working would be on that tool
finally, eventually

explanation.surface: A shoemaker seems at last to be busy.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler (shoemaker) works on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, and literally a cobbler at work stands at his shoe form.

clue.text: Big fair certain to get publicity

parts.note: an expo is a large exhibition or fair

explanation.surface: A large trade fair is bound to attract media attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage that brings something to public attention.

clue.text: Admit to being in possession

definitions.meaning: to ... up, to confess
to have something as one's property

explanation.surface: Confessing to having something.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess something is to own up, and to have property is to possess it.

clue.text: They come from remote space initially

definitions.text: They come from remote space initially

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are worked into a new form, as things that come from them
the first letter of the word space is taken

explanation.surface: Shooting stars arrive from the far reaches of space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come from' signals an anagram of REMOTE with S, the first letter of 'space'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting stars are bodies that enter the atmosphere from distant space.

clue.text: Frequently no distance at all

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means none
ft, short for foot or feet, is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: A remark that something happens often or not at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no distance at all' is zero feet: O FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word meaning often.

clue.text: Breezy letters of admiration?

parts.note: admirers' letters, with 'breezy' hinting at a device that waves air about

explanation.surface: Cheerful letters praising someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A fan both stirs a breeze and is an admirer, so admirers' letters are breezy.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent by admirers to a celebrity.

clue.text: A tattered rag more used for rapid communication

indicators.note: torn and ragged, so the letters of the words following are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tattered rag is used to send a message quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: An airmail letter-sheet was a faster way of sending a message overseas.

clue.text: Moisture laden atmosphere and corrosion create suspicion

explanation.surface: Damp air and rust together raise doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of trust, doubt about someone.

clue.text: Extend a term of imprisonment

definitions.meaning: to lengthen or draw out
slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Lengthening a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something, and slang for a period served in jail.

clue.text: Dramatic opening-of parliament?

parts.note: the opening part of a play, and a hint at the first piece of legislation passed

explanation.surface: A theatrical state opening of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: An Act of Parliament is a law, so the first one passed would also fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening division of a play, and also the first statute a legislature passes.

clue.text: One unmarried

definitions.meaning: a lone item, solitary
not wed

explanation.definitionFit: Means individual or sole, and also not wed.

clue.text: About all a gunner needs to fire

definitions.meaning: approximately, or on all sides

definitions.text: all a gunner needs to fire
definitions.meaning: one round of ammunition, all that is needed for one shot

explanation.surface: Roughly what a gunner requires to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A ROUND it is one shell or cartridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Means approximately, and split in two is one unit of ammunition.

clue.text: Outcome of partitioning Ulster

indicators.note: dividing up, so the letters of the region's name are split and rearranged

explanation.surface: A political question about the effects of dividing Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the northern province of Ireland, partitioned in 1921.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequence or effect.

clue.text: Patriotic heart of old Brazil

indicators.note: the letters at the centre of the word patriotic are taken

explanation.surface: Patriotism at the core of historic Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960, so it stands for the old nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The city was the nation's capital until Brasilia replaced it in 1960.

clue.text: Young Stanley's optimistic carriage

parts.note: Stan is the short familiar form of the name Stanley

explanation.surface: A boy called Stanley is hopeful about his vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open horse-drawn vehicle named after a nineteenth-century clergyman.

clue.text: Part of speech given by German and translated into German

parts.note: und is the German word for and, as the clue says it is translated into German

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about a German word.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal noun ending in -ing is a grammatical category.

clue.text: Lessons in draughtsmanship for the privileged

definitions.meaning: classes in drawing lines with a ruler
the elite who govern

explanation.surface: Drawing lessons for the upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruling here means drawing straight lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Classes in drawing lines, and the governing elite of a society.
